newsitem.title: UK: Butcher in court after British food poisonings.
newsitem.headline: Butcher in court after British food poisonings.

text.p: A Scottish butcher whose shop has been linked to an outbreak of food poisoning that has killed 16 people appeared in court on Friday to face a charge of "culpable and reckless conduct".

John Barr, 51, appeared briefly at Hamilton Sheriff's Court. He was committed for further examination and released on bail, according to a statement issued by the Scottish Office. No date has been set for any trial.
An outbreak of E coli poisoning among pensioners in November 1996 was traced back to meat pies supplied to a church lunch by Barr's shop in Wishaw, near Glasgow.
A second outbreak in the nearby Forth valley around the same time was not linked to the shop.
A total of 16 people have died from the two outbreaks. Several more remain ill in hospital. In all, more than 400 people are reported to have shown symptoms of E coli poisoning in the outbreak.

E coli bacteria are normally harmless but the toxic strain that killed the Scottish victims, known as 0157, can cause brain damage and kidney failure. It can be passed to humans from cattle through improper slaughtering.
